title: Ask Trellis: Unbundled Prototypes & Rapid Validation Notes
body:
Purpose and quick summary:

This is a working synthesis of customer asks that cluster around a common pattern: small, composable inference features customers want to mix-and-match (routing, short-term caching, lightweight function tooling) rather than a single large feature. I coined the shorthand 'Trellis' for the set of unbundled, minimally viable prototypes we should spin up and validate with 3 pilot customers over the next 6 weeks.

Status and ask:
- Drafting: gather quick prototypes (UI + API + minimal infra) that map to real customer vignettes.
- Goal: run 3 light validation sessions (30–45 min each) and capture success signals (time-to-result, perceived quality lift, implementation friction).
- Outcome: decide which Trellis elements to fold into backlog (priority + rough implementation estimate).

Why this cluster matters (customer evidence):
- Multiple customers (DocsFlow, NovaAssist, and one stealth startup) have asked for ways to: route to cheaper model variants if quality is acceptable; attach short-lived prefix caches for common prompts; and call tiny tools that shape output before token billing (pre-token transforms).
- Common pain: product teams don't want heavy infra changes; they want toggles and small knobs they can use in prod quickly.
- Quote excerpt from interview (DocsFlow PM): "If we could flip a knob to try a cheaper model and see how it performs on our prompts for 1 week, we'd be able to trade cost vs. accuracy ourselves."

Proposed Trellis modules (candidate prototypes):
1) QuickRoute (routing toggle)
   - UX: checkbox + confidence threshold in Console route config (can also be a per-request header).
   - Backend: policy-level routing to fallback model when latency/cost budget is low. Minimal: add a boolean flag that prefers fallback model if token estimate > X.
   - Success metric: teams can reduce per-token spend by 20% on sampled traffic without >5% perceived quality regression.

2) EphemeralPrefix (short-lived prefix caching)
   - UX: per-route prefix cache TTL control and sample inspection view.
   - Backend: leverage existing KV cache, expose a per-customer namespace with TTL override; no cross-tenant sharing.
   - Success metric: 30–40% token saving on templated prompts for pilot customers.

3) NanoTool (pre-token transformer)
   - UX: small DSL or webhook that manipulates prompt before send (e.g., sanitize, add metadata, format).
   - Backend: execute transform in sandboxed environment; ensure deterministic cost accounting (transform is free; billing only after transform).
   - Success metric: customers report fewer follow-up edits and higher first-response acceptance.

4) Lightweight AB (fast canary)
   - UX: per-route quick AB with 1-click ramp up/down, short retention of logs for validation.
   - Backend: reuse rollout infra but with much shorter retention and simpler tracing (no full eval run).
   - Success metric: teams can run quick 48–72h experiments without submitting infra tickets.

Pilot plan and timeline (6 weeks):
- Week 0: finalize scope and tech owner for each module. Align SRE/serving-runtime constraints (Devon/Rafael).
- Week 1–2: build thin Console UI and API switches. Wire up minimal backend toggles.
- Week 3: onboard 3 pilot customers, provide guided testing scripts, collect metrics.
- Week 4–5: iterate on pain-points, add lightweight telemetry hooks.
- Week 6: decision checkpoint: drop, iterate, or backlog for full productization.

Signals we'll collect (qual + quant):
- Quantitative: per-request token cost delta, avg latency delta, cache hit rate, model fallback frequency, AB uplift (if applicable).
- Qualitative: PM/engineer friction notes, usability scores from pilots, freeform feedback on control surface.

Risk and open questions (explicitly surfaced):
- Billing clarity: need a clean statement on how pre-token transforms are accounted. Legal/Finance signoff required. (Linked: CS-7421).
- Safety: EphemeralPrefix may reintroduce hallucination if prefix content is stale. Need guardrails and QA checklist.
- Resource contention: QuickRoute could increase load on fallback model; need quota/burst controls to prevent noisy neighbor effects.
- Observability: quick AB must not leak PII in short retention logs. Work with Security to ensure redaction.

Customer vignettes (short):
- DocsFlow: heavy template reuse, wants EphemeralPrefix + QuickRoute to cut cost for batch document generation.
- NovaAssist: wants NanoTool to remove PII before hitting model for regulatory reasons.
- Stealth startup: wants Lightweight AB to test a cheaper model variant on 5% of traffic and see customer complaints.

Notes on measurement and validation scripts (sample):
- Validation step 1: Baseline run for 3 days (collect tokens per session, failures, NPS-lite).
- Validation step 2: Enable Trellis module at 10% sample for 48h, collect same metrics.
- Validation step 3: Guided interview with PM/engineer to capture subjective assessment.

Implementation rough estimates (engineering appetite):
- QuickRoute: 2 sprints (1 infra + 1 console + light tracing) if we scope to policy flag only.
- EphemeralPrefix: 2–3 sprints (cache namespacing, UI, safety checks).
- NanoTool: 1–2 sprints for a limited webhook runner and safe sandbox; more if DSL expands.
- Lightweight AB: 1 sprint to expose existing rollout with shorter retention settings.

Next steps (owner: Maya):
- Confirm tech owners and SRE gate conditions by 2026-10-12.
- Draft pilot invites and one-pager for pilot customers.
- Schedule 30m sync with Finance and Security to unblock billing & redaction questions.

Appendix (quick links and artifacts):
- Pilot script template (in Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/CS/Ask-Trellis-Overview
- Related Jira: CS-7421 (billing), CS-7499 (prefix safety), CS-7588 (console tiny UX).
- Experimental PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/3345

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep prototypes deliberately small. Avoid full eval pipeline in pilot — we need speed.
- Ask pilot PMs to give an internal champion so we get real usage signals, not just a demo.
- Track cost delta per 10k tokens as the primary go/no-go metric for QuickRoute and EphemeralPrefix.

Unresolved decisions for next sync:
- Exact TTL floor for EphemeralPrefix (1 hour vs 6 hours).
- Whether NanoTool runs synchronously or as a pre-processing step in edge.
- SRE limits to allow for on-demand fallback ramps.

End of notes.
